Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the guest journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it. Each dot is one automation.

1

Discover and inquire

Guests compare hotels, menus, tours and venues on Google, OTAs, aggregators and social media, then message the business directly. Fast answers with real prices and availability decide who gets the booking, and whether it comes direct.

Touchpoints

  • Google Business Profile and search
  • OTA and food aggregator listings
  • Instagram and WhatsApp messages
  • Website chat and booking engine
  • Phone and email inquiries

Accountable owner

Reservations or sales lead

Automations on this stage

  • Discover and inquireDirect booking inquiry deskAnswer room inquiries from WhatsApp, Instagram, website chat and email with live rates and availability, offer a direct booking link, and pass group, long-stay and corporate requests to sales with the details already captured.3–5 weeks
  • Discover and inquireOTA rate consistency watchCheck every day that the prices guests see on OTAs and metasearch match what the hotel loaded, flag undercuts and stale inventory, and give the revenue manager a short exception list instead of a spreadsheet to scan.3–4 weeks
  • Discover and inquireAggregator menu sync and rating watchKeep Swiggy, Zomato and other ordering channels in step with what the kitchen can actually make, and give each brand and outlet a daily digest of ratings, complaints and the dishes behind them.3–5 weeks
2

Quote, confirm and pay

Inquiries become reservations, quotes, proposals and tentative holds. Availability, pricing rules, approvals and advance payments meet here, and slow or inconsistent handling is where most revenue is lost.

Touchpoints

  • Group RFPs and event proposals
  • Table reservations and waitlists
  • Itinerary quotes
  • Tentative holds and contracts
  • Advance payment links

Accountable owner

Sales or reservations manager

Automations on this stage

  • Quote, confirm and payGroup, MICE and wedding inquiry deskTurn group RFPs, corporate offsites and wedding inquiries into qualified opportunities with a checked date, a tentative hold that expires on schedule, and a proposal draft built from approved packages for the sales manager to finalize.5–8 weeks
  • Quote, confirm and payTable reservations, reminders and waitlistTake bookings from WhatsApp, Instagram, the website, reservation partners and the Google Business Profile booking link into one book, confirm and remind guests on the day, run a fair walk-in waitlist with table-ready messages, and record no-shows for next time.2–4 weeks
  • Quote, confirm and payInquiry-to-itinerary quote with an AI first draftTurn a traveler's inquiry into a structured brief, assemble a first-draft itinerary from the agency's own past trips and current supplier rates, and let a travel consultant check, price and send it.6–8 weeks
3

Prepare for arrival

Between booking and arrival, guests need the right information at the right time, and the business needs details, documents, payments and vendor confirmations before the day. Most day-of problems can be prevented here.

Touchpoints

  • Pre-arrival WhatsApp messages
  • Pre-check-in form and ID details
  • Travel document and visa checklists
  • Vendor briefs and final guest counts
  • Instalment reminders

Accountable owner

Front office, operations or event manager

Automations on this stage

  • Prepare for arrivalPre-arrival messages, digital pre-check-in and Form III supportSend each booked guest an approved pre-arrival WhatsApp message with a secure pre-check-in link, collect arrival time, ID details and consented extras before arrival, and give the front desk a verified queue and a Form III deadline tracker.5–7 weeks
  • Prepare for arrivalTrip readiness: documents, visas and payment milestonesGive every booked traveler a clear checklist of documents, visa steps and payment dates, send reminders before each cut-off, collect instalments through gateway links, and alert the consultant when anything is late.3–5 weeks
  • Prepare for arrivalEvent planning, vendor coordination and run sheetOnce an event is confirmed, track vendor tasks, client decisions, instalments and the final guest count against deadlines, then generate the event-day run sheet and function sheets from the same record.4–6 weeks
4

Stay, dine, travel or celebrate

The stay, the meal, the trip or the event itself, plus the floor operations that keep it on track: guest requests and their response targets, live itinerary changes, and the kitchen's daily close.

Touchpoints

  • In-stay requests by WhatsApp or room QR code
  • Housekeeping and maintenance tickets
  • Daily itinerary and flight change messages
  • Kitchen close, wastage and stock counts

Accountable owner

Duty manager or operations head

Automations on this stage

  • Stay, dine, travel or celebrateIn-stay request routing with SLA alertsLet guests send requests on WhatsApp or through a room QR code, turn each into a ticket for housekeeping, maintenance, food and beverage or the front desk, and escalate to the duty manager when a response target is missed.4–6 weeks
  • Stay, dine, travel or celebrateLive trip updates and on-trip supportKeep travelers informed during the trip with evening-before itinerary messages, pickup details and flight change alerts, and route any problem to the duty consultant with the booking context attached.4–6 weeks
  • Stay, dine, travel or celebrateOutlet daily close: sales, settlements and wastageEach morning, combine POS sales, aggregator orders and payouts, stock counts and wastage logs into one report per outlet and brand, with exceptions flagged for the owner and the accounts team.4–6 weeks
5

Feedback and recovery

After checkout, the meal, the trip or the event, private feedback gives a chance to fix problems, and public reviews shape the next guest's choice. Every guest is asked the same way and every public reply has an approver.

Touchpoints

  • Private feedback form
  • Service recovery calls and messages
  • Google, OTA and aggregator reviews
  • Review replies

Accountable owner

Guest relations manager

Automations on this stage

  • Feedback and recoveryFeedback, service recovery and review repliesAsk every guest for private feedback after a stay, meal, trip or event, open a recovery case when something went wrong, invite every guest to review without filtering, and draft replies to public reviews for a manager to approve.3–5 weeks
6

Return and refer

Regulars, repeat travelers and annual event clients are the most valuable guests. Consented, relevant offers and timely reminders bring them back without mass promotions that break messaging rules or erode trust.

Touchpoints

  • Loyalty points and visit rewards
  • Birthday and anniversary messages
  • Win-back offers for lapsed guests
  • Annual corporate event reminders

Accountable owner

Marketing or CRM lead

Automations on this stage

  • Return and referRepeat guest, loyalty and win-back programUse visit and booking history to recognize regulars, send consented offers on occasions that matter to each guest, invite lapsed guests back, and remind sales ahead of corporate clients' annual events.4–6 weeks

Where people stay in control

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Direct booking inquiry deskDiscover and inquireReservations staff own any negotiated rate, discount, group quote or exception to policy. The assistant shares only rates and availability returned by the booking engine and hands over when it is unsure or the guest asks for a person.
OTA rate consistency watchDiscover and inquireThe revenue manager decides every rate change and every conversation with an OTA or wholesaler. The automation never changes rates, restrictions or inventory on its own.
Aggregator menu sync and rating watchDiscover and inquireThe outlet manager confirms switch-offs for items outside a pre-approved list and owns every response to complaints. Food safety complaints go straight to the outlet's food safety supervisor or owner and are never closed by automation.
Group, MICE and wedding inquiry deskQuote, confirm and payThe sales manager approves fit, pricing, concessions and the proposal before it goes out, and the revenue manager signs off room block rates on high-demand dates. Contract and cancellation terms are confirmed by the person authorized to sign.
Table reservations, reminders and waitlistQuote, confirm and payThe host or floor manager decides seating, overbooking on peak nights and any deposit or cancellation charge. Deposit and cancellation policies are written by the owner and shown to guests before they book.
Inquiry-to-itinerary quote with an AI first draftQuote, confirm and payA travel consultant checks every hotel, transfer and price, confirms availability with suppliers and approves the quote before it reaches the traveler. Visa and health guidance in a quote comes only from the consultant, never from the model.
Pre-arrival messages, digital pre-check-in and Form III supportPrepare for arrivalFront desk staff check the original ID or passport at arrival before anything is filed, and a named front office user submits Form III on the Bureau of Immigration portal. Extras that need a decision, such as early check-in on a full night, are confirmed by the front office manager.
Trip readiness: documents, visas and payment milestonesPrepare for arrivalConsultants maintain destination checklists from official embassy and visa center sources and confirm visa requirements with each traveler; the automation sends reminders, not advice. Finance owns tax treatment such as TCS on overseas packages, refunds and any change to the payment schedule.
Event planning, vendor coordination and run sheetPrepare for arrivalThe event manager approves the final run sheet, any change after the guest count cut-off and any vendor substitution. The venue's licensing and safety owner confirms permits such as liquor, music and fire approvals before the event.
In-stay request routing with SLA alertsStay, dine, travel or celebrateDepartment staff resolve and close tickets. The duty manager owns escalations, anything involving safety, security or health, and any compensation. Guests can ask for a person at any point in the conversation.
Live trip updates and on-trip supportStay, dine, travel or celebrateThe duty consultant handles every problem, rebooking, refund or safety concern; the automation only shares confirmed itinerary information. Emergencies are escalated by phone to the on-call manager.
Outlet daily close: sales, settlements and wastageStay, dine, travel or celebrateThe outlet manager confirms wastage entries and explains variances. The accountant reviews settlement differences and GST reporting before filing and raises disputes with aggregators.
Feedback, service recovery and review repliesFeedback and recoveryA named manager edits and approves every public reply and decides every refund, compensation or goodwill gesture. Allegations involving safety, health, discrimination or legal threats go to the general manager or owner before any response.
Repeat guest, loyalty and win-back programReturn and referThe marketing owner approves segments, offers and every template. The sales manager personally handles outreach to corporate and event clients. Discounts beyond agreed limits need owner approval.
